title: Petroleum Facilities Guard Blocks Zawiya Refinery and Brega Marketing Gates, NOC Prepares Force Majeure
detail: Members of the Petroleum Facilities Guard blocked the main gates of the Zawiya Oil Refining Company and the Brega Petroleum Marketing Company on Tuesday morning, September 22, 2026, preventing staff and technicians from entering and blocking the relief of night-shift crews, the National Oil Corporation (NOC) said. The blockade compounded the ongoing closure of Valve No. 7 on the Hamada-area Sharara pipeline — attributed to PFG personnel from the southwest region alongside an unnamed armed group — with roughly 130,000 bpd offline from Sharara and rising if the closure continued. The NOC called on those responsible to 'immediately reopen all gates' and warned continued obstruction risked 'complete operational paralysis' of the Zawiya complex, saying its board was prepared to declare force majeure to meet contractual obligations if the valve did not reopen. By Wednesday, September 23, the Brega Company's gate had been partially reopened, but the main gate to the Zawiya Refinery remained closed and no force majeure declaration had yet been confirmed.

media.caption: Zawiya Oil Refining Company complex; Petroleum Facilities Guard members blocked its main gate and Brega Marketing's gate, prompting an NOC force-majeure warning, Sep 22, 2026

confidenceReason: The gate blockade, NOC's demand to reopen, and the force-majeure warning are reported directly by Libya Update citing the NOC statement, independently corroborated by Arab News' separate report of the same shutdown; the partial Sep 23 reopening of the Brega gate is reported by Libya Update alone and noted here as a single-source follow-up.
